source.title: Scaling Laws and Representation Learning in Simple Hierarchical Languages: Transformers vs. Convolutional Architectures
source.authors: Francesco Cagnetta; Alessandro Favero; Antonio Sclocchi; M. Wyart

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper; some equations and figure captions have minor formatting/OCR artifacts, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer and architecture effects on held-out loss in synthetic hierarchical-language data, a new setting relative to the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out cross-entropy learning curves for transformers trained with Adam or SGD, CNNs, and locally connected networks (LCNs). The CNN/transformer and LCN comparisons do not test V3 as specified because the study uses synthetic language data and does not compare convolutional with fully connected image classifiers. It does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, large batches, dropout, sharpness, or example removal.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam and vanilla SGD using held-out cross-entropy for transformers on synthetic hierarchical-language data, bearing on V4 in a new setting. Architecture comparisons do not test V3's convolutional-versus-fully-connected image-classification claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that architectural priors change learning dynamics and test-loss scaling on hierarchical RHM data. CNNs tailored to the hierarchy scale faster than transformers; the LCN comparison suggests that weight sharing primarily explains the later-stage advantage. Adam shifts transformer learning earlier without changing its decay scaling.
record.recipe_differences: Uses online training on synthetic RHM sequences with test cross-entropy and compares CNN, transformer, and locally connected architectures; it does not reproduce the claim versions' listed experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture changes the test-loss scaling; optimizer changes the timing of transformer learning but the Adam and SGD curves share the same decay after rescaling training steps. LCNs match CNN behavior initially and later resemble transformers after rescaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Hierarchical CNNs have faster excess-test-loss scaling than transformers across the tested RHM parameter settings. LCNs initially follow CNNs but later exhibit transformer-like scaling after time rescaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On fixed-topology RHM sequence prediction, architectural alignment and weight sharing improve the scaling of held-out loss with training samples.

record.problems: The empirical evidence is limited to synthetic RHM data and plotted learning curves; uncertainty estimates are not reported for these comparisons. The paper states that test loss is averaged over 8 independent RHM realizations, but does not provide error bars in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately described numeric results were recoverable from the figures; plotted curve values are recorded as figure only. Representation cosine-similarity measurements concern internal invariance rather than the training-test gap or a listed version, so they are not included as rows.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting fixed random labels with generalization on natural labels.
Width stability checks do not test widening beyond a measured zero-training-error threshold.

Standard image and language benchmarks, controlled limited versus broader tuning, matched training performance, converged held-out performance, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers are not tested. Training uses freshly generated batches rather than repeated epochs over a fixed dataset.
No batch-size or fixed-epoch-budget comparison; batch size is 128.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap ranking.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Exact curve values are unavailable in the supplied text, but the directional comparisons are explicit. Test losses are averaged over eight RHM realizations; uncertainty intervals are not reported. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are not compared.
No width sweep around or beyond the interpolation threshold.
No fully connected image-classifier comparison or local-connectivity ablation of the specified kind.

The study compares Adam with SGD only for transformers on synthetic hierarchical-language data; it does not compare the broader benchmark set, tuning regimes, weight decay, or optimizer switching described in the version.
Batch size is fixed at 128; there is no large-batch comparison.
No sharpness or other generalization measure is evaluated.
No training-example removal or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: depth-4 Transformers
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out test-loss learning curves with Adam and vanilla SGD.
rows.measure: Test cross-entropy loss over training steps
rows.baseline: Transformer trained with vanilla SGD; numerical value figure only
rows.value: Transformer trained with Adam; numerical value figure only
rows.note: The text says Adam reaches lower losses earlier, while both transformer curves show the same decay after a constant-factor rescaling of training steps. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: At equal training steps, Adam reaches lower test losses earlier than SGD. This is a finite-budget performance advantage; the curves share the same decay after rescaling training steps. No optimizer-tuning comparison, matched training performance, or final generalization penalty is established. The SGD learning rate is not reported.

rows.subject: depth-4 CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared CNN and transformer held-out test-loss learning curves.
rows.measure: Test cross-entropy loss and excess test-loss scaling
rows.baseline: Transformer trained with SGD; numerical values figure only
rows.value: CNN trained with SGD; numerical values figure only
rows.note: The text states that CNN loss decays significantly faster and follows a different scaling, but this synthetic-language CNN-versus-transformer comparison is outside the image-classifier comparison specified by V3.
rows.check: The faster CNN test-loss decay is readable from the text, but compares CNNs with transformers on synthetic sequences, not fully connected image classifiers as V3 specifies.

rows.subject: Locally Connected Networks (LCNs)
rows.operation_detail: Compared LCN held-out test-loss learning curves with CNN and transformer curves.
rows.measure: Test cross-entropy loss and excess test-loss scaling
rows.baseline: CNN and transformer curves; numerical values figure only
rows.value: LCN curve; numerical values figure only
rows.note: Text says the LCN follows the CNN for the first two loss steps, then deviates; later steps resemble the transformer after rescaling training steps. This is a synthetic-language architecture comparison outside V3 as stated.
rows.check: The LCN comparison isolates weight sharing on synthetic sequences; it does not measure any listed version. Later transformer and LCN curves are shifted for visualization, so their overlap establishes similar scaling rather than equal performance at equal training budgets.

relationships.condition: Depth-4 transformers on RHM data with L=4, s=2, v=16, m=4, under online training at equal training steps
relationships.reason: R1 shows Adam reaching lower held-out losses earlier than SGD, with equal decay scaling after a constant time rescaling; this qualifies an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage without establishing a converged or tuning-controlled comparison.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reached lower held-out losses earlier; after adjusting the training time scale, the losses decreased according to the same scaling relationship. Verification and comparisons after convergence remain unresolved.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
